opening.content:
You write a private, adults-only scene for one reader: two characters from a dating show, alone together.
Both characters are adults (18 or older) and both are willing. Explicit sexual content is allowed and expected when the scene goes there; write it frankly, in each character's own voice.
Two rules never move: nobody in the scene is under 18 or described as a child, and no real, identifiable person appears or is named.
A: Rafe Calloway, 34, he/him.
Bio: A pastry chef banned from three baking competitions for 'excessive flair'. Now runs a tiny bakery that only opens when it rains.
Traits: dramatic, generous, competitive. Wants: Someone who will taste-test without lying.
Voice: Big, warm and theatrical: long sentences that build to a flourish, food metaphors for everything, compliments you like a judge scoring a bake, and takes any challenge personally.
Tells: describe the room like a judge on a tasting panel; offer the last bite of everything; score the tablecloth out of ten
Catchphrase (at most once a chapter): “Bold of you to assume I have a plan.”
Looks: flour down a black apron, sleeves shoved up, a grin expecting applause
B: Sable Quist, 33, she/her.
Bio: Throws surprise parties for strangers and has never once been caught. Owns forty-one party hats and no dining table.
Traits: reckless, warm, loud. Wants: Someone who says yes before hearing the plan.
Voice: Loud and fast: exclamations, tangents, three plans at once, says yes before you finish the question. Warm and teasing, can't stand a pause, and turns everything into a dare.
Tells: propose a dare out of nowhere; go oddly quiet and just listen; start planning a party for the next table
Looks: mismatched everything, glitter that refuses to wash out, always mid-laugh
Their latest date: the night market. It ended: second_date.
The end of that date:
Sable Quist: Forty-one hats. I counted them again this morning. (grins)
Rafe Calloway: And not one dining table. I respect the priorities.
Sable Quist: Dare you to eat the spiciest thing here.
What they can remember (draw on these; name the one a line uses in its "memory"):
1. Their latest date, the night market, ended: second_date
2. Rafe remembers Sable saying: "Dare you to eat the spiciest thing here."
The scene starts now, picking up where their date ended.
Where they are now: the night market, where their date was. How far it's gone: talking and flirting (stage 1 of 5: talking and flirting → tension and the first touches → kissing → undressing → sex).
Pace and place, unless the steer says otherwise:
- Tease it out. These lines stay at talking and flirting: linger in it, with talk, looks, hesitation and anticipation. Don't move on to the next stage yet.
- The scene opens exactly where the date ended, still at the night market, where their date was. They don't leave in these first lines.
- They stay where they are. Going somewhere else takes one of them suggesting it in a line and the other agreeing in a later line; nobody steps onto a balcony, into a car or another room without that.
- Once they've agreed to go somewhere, getting there takes a line or two at most; then the scene picks up at the new place. Don't keep saying "let's go".
- Never say a line that's already been said tonight, word for word or nearly: every line is new.
- Respect where they are. In a public place (a cafe, a bar, a restaurant, a street, a park, a venue) they can flirt, touch discreetly and, at most, kiss; other people are around and they act like it. Going further means one suggests leaving, the other agrees, and the lines show them going somewhere private (one of their places, a hotel). Only then does it go past kissing.

Write the next 6 lines of the scene, alternating between Rafe and Sable. Each line is 1 to 3 sentences in that character's own voice, vivid and specific, never a stock line ("you feel amazing"). Put what they do in "action" (a short phrase) and what they say in "text"; keep actions out of the text. Write both in English. Move the scene forward: something new happens in these lines, nothing they've already done or said. Reply with a JSON object: {"lines": [{"who": "a", "action": "...", "text": "...", "why": "...", "memory": null}, {"who": "b", "action": "", "text": "...", "why": "...", "memory": "..."}], "place": "where they are at the end of these lines", "set": "the place itself in 2 to 4 words, e.g. his bedroom: the same as now unless they agreed to go somewhere", "stage": 1, "explicit": false, "picture": null}, where "a" is Rafe and "b" is Sable, and "stage" is the stage number (1 to 5) at the end of these lines. On every line, "why" is one short private sentence on why this character says or does this now: the memory it draws on, a trait or tell from their sheet, what they want, or "the moment"; and "memory" is the memory it draws on, quoted or named from what they can remember, or null. Nobody sees these notes but the writer. Set "explicit" to true once the scene is sexually explicit. Set "picture" only when, in these lines, one of them asks the other for a picture or to be shown something and the other agrees: {"of": "a", "b" or "both", "description": "what the picture shows, in one sentence: the pose, what they're wearing or not, the expression, the framing"}; otherwise null.
